resources.string: Hardware keys, vibrator patterns, notification LED
InputManager lists no device: inputflinger is not running or /dev/input is not accessible.

No input device reports a touchscreen source: the touch driver did not probe (check dmesg for the touch IC, firmware loading, regulators and GPIOs in the device tree) or its IDC file declares the wrong device type.
The volume keys are not in any key layout: the gpio-keys or PMIC key driver is not registered, or the .kl file maps scan codes 114/115 to something else.
POWER is not in any key layout: the PMIC power-on key driver (qpnp-power-on / pon) is missing or its .kl file does not map scan code 116.
Phones normally have one: the vibrator HAL (android.hardware.vibrator) is missing, or the kernel driver (qpnp-haptic, timed_output or the leds \"vibrator\" class) did not probe.
No composition primitives: the vibrator HAL only plays on/off waveforms (common on older devices).
%1$d LEDs in sysfs, no notification LED
No red/green/blue or indicator LED in /sys/class/leds. Many phones have none; if this one does, its driver did not probe or uses another name the lights HAL must know.
Each key is ticked and saved as soon as it is seen.
Start the test, then press every physical key. For Power, press it once: the screen turning off counts.
Listening: keys do nothing else while the test runs (no volume panel). Back is recorded too; use Stop to finish.
Two-stage camera key (Lumia): half-press sends FOCUS, full press sends CAMERA. Both should appear.
Basic patterns, predefined effects and primitives.
No amplitude control: every vibration has the same strength, so the ramp is not offered.
Effects marked \"no\" or \"unknown\" fall back to a plain pulse emulated by the framework.
Nothing at all? Check that vibration is not turned off in Settings › Sound & vibration.
Did every button vibrate, with the ramp getting stronger towards the end?
Kernel LEDs and a test notification that asks for a coloured light.
No LED class devices are readable.
Choose a colour, tap the button and turn the screen off within %1$d s: most ROMs light the LED only while the screen is off.
Notification posted. Turn the screen on again when you have looked at the LED.
The lights HAL drove these kernel LEDs:
No kernel LED changed: the lights HAL did not drive any LED (missing lights HAL, wrong LED names, SELinux denials on the sysfs nodes), or the device has no LED.
The notification LED should now blink. Colour: %1$s.
Did the LED blink in the chosen colour while the screen was off?
